issue.title: GitHub deploy-key refusals ('denied to deploy key') are not classified as credential failures
issue.description:
GitHub refuses a push made with a deploy key scoped to a different repository with
`ERROR: Permission to <owner>/<repo>.git denied to deploy key` (then `fatal: Could not
read from remote repository.`). None of SASE's git-failure classifiers recognize that
text as a credential failure, and the service-host readiness warning words it wrongly.

Root cause (traced, not inferred):

1. `sase-core` `crates/sase_core/src/retryability/mod.rs` `AUTH_MARKERS` contains
   `permission denied (publickey)` but no marker for `denied to deploy key`, so
   `classify_failure_retryability(RETRY_OPERATION_GIT, ...)` returns a non-credential
   verdict. Downstream, `src/sase/workspace_provider/_lease_git.py`
   `_preparation_error` skips `_with_ssh_agent_hint`, and the external issue mirror's
   `auth_error` classification and backoff never apply.
2. `src/sase/bead/_sync_logs.py` labels failures `credential failure` only on
   contiguous `permission denied` / `publickey` / `authentication` / ..., so
   `permission to ... denied to deploy key` falls through to `other failure`.
3. Commit 8c4acffdb made `probe_git_remote_auth` return `denied` for a deploy-key
   greeting (`Hi <owner>/<repo>!`). But `ssh_agent_readiness_warnings` /
   `_agent_detail` in `src/sase/service/ssh_agent.py` still say "the SSH agent at X
   holds identities, but the remote accepted none" and "will fail with `Permission
   denied (publickey)`". For this case, both statements are false: the remote
   accepted a deploy key, and pushes fail with `denied to deploy key`. The fix should
   name the greeted repository and point at `IdentitiesOnly yes`, for example by
   returning the greeted login from a private probe helper. It must keep the
   `probe_git_remote_auth` API and the never-raising contract.

Fix direction: add a `denied to deploy key` marker (and, carefully, the
`permission to ` + ` denied to ` shape) to the Rust `AUTH_MARKERS` with a retryability
test, update Python callers or pins as the core-boundary rule requires, extend the
`_sync_logs.py` matcher, and give the deploy-key readiness warning accurate wording
with tests in `tests/service/test_service_effective_env.py`.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every deploy-key refusal is diagnosed as a generic git failure. Lease errors lose the
SSH-credential remediation hint, the external issue mirror retries without `auth_error`
backoff, bead-sync logs call it `other failure`, and `sase service status` (after
8c4acffdb) points users at an empty agent instead of the deploy key that is actually
answering. Today's incident was only diagnosed by hand.
task_type_fields.location: sase-core retryability AUTH_MARKERS; src/sase/bead/_sync_logs.py classify_sync_error; src/sase/service/ssh_agent.py _agent_detail
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed live on athena, 2026-09-22 08:02-08:09 EDT. After the 06:31 reboot,
`ssh-add-all` loaded `~/.ssh/id_bob_vault` (a deploy key for `bobs-org/bob`) first
into the login ssh-agent, and `Host github.com` had no `IdentitiesOnly`. Every
`github.com` push from ACE-launched agents then failed. research.27.gem and
research.27.mus failed at `sase stitch create --resume` with `Permission to
sase-org/sase--research.git denied to deploy key`. 0p2--mon failed epic graph
publication with `Permission to sase-org/sase--beads.git denied to deploy key`.
`ssh -T git@github.com` answered `Hi bobs-org/bob! You've successfully authenticated`.

Offline reproduction (run 2026-09-22 against installed sase-core):
`classify_failure_retryability(RETRY_OPERATION_GIT, exit_status=128, stderr="ERROR: Permission to o/r.git denied to deploy key\nfatal: Could not read from remote repository.\n")`
returns `verdict='permanent', reason='unclassified: failure did not match a retryable signature'`,
so `is_credential_verdict(...)` is False, and `sase.bead._sync_logs.classify_sync_error(...)`
returns `'other failure'`. The same call with `Permission denied (publickey)` returns
`reason='authentication: ...'`, `is_credential_verdict` True, `'credential failure'`.
